title: The exit-5 conflict names a cause it has not established and never echoes the revision the caller sent
description:
Measured on dev (0.12.0) 2026-09-30 in a scratch workspace (mktemp + git init + quest init, never a live record), reproducing the lore-cli report against 0.11.0. The guard itself is correct; the conflict MESSAGE and its input are what cannot be trusted.

Positive control and finding, same invocation: sending the exact current revision exits 0. Empty string, deadbeef, the literal string null, and a genuinely stale revision all exit 5 with a byte-identical body whose input carries ONLY actualRevision -- the current revision -- and never the value that was sent. A sentinel string passed as the precondition appears 0 times anywhere in the error body.

Consequence, which is what makes this worse than merely unhelpful: the only revision in the error is the current one, so anyone who transcribes "the revision" out of it reproduces sent == actual exactly. That is how the original report arose.

Source: src/cli/main.ts:4173-4183 attaches only input.actualRevision. The sibling branch at src/cli/main.ts:4184-4201 (tracker_write_conflict, dependency_target_ambiguous, task_already_exists) emits the identical message with no input at all, so a caller cannot tell a failed precondition from another writer winning either.

Contributing trap from the same measurement: task create --json and task list --json carry no revision field at all (only task view does), so jq -r .data.revision prints null, and feeding that null to the precondition produces exactly this opaque exit 5.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A conflict whose sent revision never matched anything names the cause it established -- a mismatch between the sent value and the current revision -- instead of asserting the record changed concurrently
The conflict error carries the revision the caller sent beside actualRevision, so sent-versus-actual is a comparison the caller can make without reconstructing argv
A guarded-precondition failure is distinguishable from the revision-less conflicts (tracker_write_conflict, dependency_target_ambiguous, task_already_exists) that currently emit a byte-identical body
Verified against the built platform binary as well as the dev source, since the defect ships in the released CLI and reproduces on 0.11.0

plan: 1. Mark the if-revision guard conflict at its source (an internal conflict-cause code on TaskWriteConflict) and carry it plus the sent revision through TrackerWriteConflictError to the CLI classifier.

2. Split the TrackerWriteConflictError branch in src/cli/main.ts: guarded-precondition failures get a message naming the established mismatch, a re-read hint, and input {sentRevision, actualRevision}; writer races keep today message and input {actualRevision}.
3. Update the --if-revision help prose for the echoed pair.

4. New test/qcli425: control exit 0; guarded failure echoes the exact sentinel plus actual; empty-string sent echoed; distinguishability from a writer-race conflict; defect reproduced on the built 0.12.0 binary and installed 0.11.0; fixed tree compiled to /tmp and exercised end to end.
5. bun run check under pinned 1.4.2; branch, PR, required checks, merge.
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-30 (session 8e31abf1). Measured first, on three forms, all identical: the dev source, the built 0.12.0 platform binary (npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest) and the installed 0.11.0. A guarded edit whose --if-revision matches nothing exits 5 with message "Task state changed concurrently" -- a cause the guard never established -- and input carrying only actualRevision; a sentinel sent value appears zero times anywhere; empty-string, literal-null and sentinel bodies are byte-identical (cmp). Reproduced exactly as recorded, including the transcription trap: the only revision in the body is the current one.

THE CHANGE. The guard's refusal is now marked at its source. TaskWriteConflict gains an optional code: "revision_precondition_failed", set where the comparison is made in tasks.ts, because a workspace CAS race produces the same interface with expectedRevision holding a snapshot revision rather than anything a caller sent -- consumers must key on the code, never on expectedRevision. TrackerWriteConflictError carries sentRevision (present only for that code) beside actualRevision, and the CLI classifier splits the branch: the guarded failure names the established mismatch ("does not match the record's current revision ... Nothing was written.") with a re-read-and-retry hint and input {sentRevision, actualRevision}; every other conflict keeps the concurrent-change wording and input {actualRevision}. The --if-revision help prose documents the echoed pair.

CONTRACT AUDIT, deliberate: every machine-visible change is message prose or an ADDITIVE key inside the existing input object -- no error_type change, no exit-code change, no top-level envelope key. Routed to opum-agent with the measurement before implementation; they read it as the wording/echo case and said proceed.

VERIFIED. test/qcli425-conflict-cause-and-echo.test.ts, four CLI-level tests: the control still exits 0; a sentinel failure names the mismatch and not the concurrent wording, echoes sentRevision equal to the sentinel and actualRevision equal to the re-read revision, contains the sentinel exactly once, and a retry with the echoed actualRevision succeeds; an empty-string sent value is echoed as "" rather than swallowed; and a 16-writer race keeps the concurrent wording with no sentRevision, so guarded failures and race conflicts are distinguishable. Mutation: reverting only the source while keeping the tests reddens exactly the predicted subset -- the two echo tests plus the service-level guard test's code assertion -- 32 pass, 3 fail; restored, 35 of 35 across the three affected files. Full bun run check under pinned bun 1.4.2: 1067 pass, 0 fail, typecheck/lint/format/layers clean.

AC4, clause by clause, so the reading is auditable. The DEFECT was reproduced against the built 0.12.0 platform binary and the installed 0.11.0 (byte-identical bodies to the dev source's). The FIX was verified on the dev source through the suite, and against a binary compiled from the fixed tree (bun build --compile to /tmp: control exit 0, sentinel failure carrying both revisions with the new message) -- the committed platform binary still carries the pre-fix bytes by construction and receives the fix at the next release. The batch route's per-item guard is untouched and deliberately out of scope: it already names expected and actual in its message and is a validation error (exit 6), not this conflict.
finalSummary: The exit-5 conflict now names the cause it established and echoes the sent revision. The --if-revision guard's refusal is marked at its source (TaskWriteConflict code revision_precondition_failed), carried through TrackerWriteConflictError as sentRevision beside actualRevision, and the classifier gives it its own message (the sent/current mismatch, Nothing was written) with input {sentRevision, actualRevision} and a re-read-and-retry hint; writer races keep the concurrent-change wording and carry no sentRevision, so the two are distinguishable. Every machine-visible change is prose or an additive key inside input -- no error_type, exit-code or top-level change; routed to opum-agent, who read it as the wording/echo case before implementation. Verified by four CLI-level tests (control; sentinel echo incl. exactly-once and successful retry with the echoed revision; empty-string echo; 16-writer race distinguishability), a mutation reddening exactly the predicted subset, the full check (1067 pass, 0 fail), the defect reproduced on the built 0.12.0 binary and 0.11.0, and the fix exercised through a binary compiled from the fixed tree.
